ali-olympic-cauldron-atlanta.fact: Ali, who had Parkinson's disease, lit the cauldron after a relay of more than 10,000 torchbearers. The stadium was later reconfigured for the Atlanta Braves.
ali-olympic-cauldron-atlanta.note: trembling hands kept implicitly via Parkinson's; cauldron-survives claim not supported by Centennial Olympic Stadium, opening ceremony or Center Parc Stadium articles

montgomery-bus-boycott-church.note: checked against Holt Street Baptist Church

pont-du-gard-aqueduct.fact: The bridge carried the Nîmes aqueduct across the Gardon valley and, standing 48.8 m high, is one of the best preserved Roman aqueduct bridges.
pont-du-gard-aqueduct.note: "tallest Roman aqueduct bridge still standing" not in the article (article: one of the best preserved, 48.8 m)

meteora-greece.fact: Meteora's monastic community began forming in the 14th century; six of its 24 monasteries survive, listed by UNESCO in 1988.
meteora-greece.note: "six remain active today" contradicted by the article (four occupied as of December 2025; six extant)

our-lady-peace-basilica.note: checked against Basilica of Our Lady of Peace

tatev-gorge-monastery.note: clue said "once reached"; the Wings of Tatev tramway opened in 2010 and still runs

zipaquira-salt-cathedral.note: checked against Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá

brimstone-hill-fortress.note: checked against Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park

katskhi-pillar-hermitage.fact: Religious buildings have occupied the pillar since at least the early medieval period; an iron ladder climbs it, though visitors have been barred since 2012.
katskhi-pillar-hermitage.note: "modern access is by a metal ladder" outdated (visitors barred since 2012)

banteay-chhmar-face-towers.fact: Built under Jayavarman VII in the Bayon style, it flourished in the 12th and 13th centuries, though looters have since stripped many of its reliefs.
banteay-chhmar-face-towers.note: battle and daily-life relief claim not in the article

humberstone-saltpeter-works.note: checked against Humberstone and Santa Laura Saltpeter Works

larnach-castle-otago.fact: Built from 1871 for a merchant and politician, the Gothic Revival house mixes local basalt and timber with materials imported from around the world.
larnach-castle-otago.note: "locally sourced stone and timber" half true (article: imported materials from around the world, Italian marble, Venetian glass)

pudong-cn.fact: Pudong was mostly farmland before its development began in 1990 and now holds Shanghai's famous skyline, including the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Shanghai Tower.
pudong-cn.note: "farmland until 1990" overstated (mainly farmland with wharfs and warehouses; development policy announced 1990)

luoyang-cn.fact: Luoyang is the earliest of China's Four Great Ancient Capitals and lies near the Longmen Grottoes, packed with Buddhist carvings.
luoyang-cn.note: "capital for over a dozen dynasties" not stated in the article

muscat.fact: This port between rugged mountains and the sea has been a leading trading port since the early 1st century CE.
muscat.note: "more than two millennia" overstated (article: known since the early 1st century CE)

lake-titicaca.fact: At about 3,812 meters above sea level, it is often called the world's highest navigable lake.
lake-titicaca.note: "used by large commercial vessels" qualifier not in the article; article: often called the highest navigable lake

banff.fact: This resort town, 1,400 to 1,630 m up, sits inside the country's oldest national park amid turquoise lakes and Rocky Mountain peaks.

mont-blanc.fact: Mont Blanc is the highest mountain in the Alps (about 4,807 m).
